A.explanation: All particles in one loop between successive nodes move up together and down together, so they have the same phase.

B.explanation: At an antinode the two creating waves reinforce, so the maximum amplitude is twice, not equal to, the amplitude $a$ of one wave.

C.explanation: The separation of two adjacent nodes is only half a loop, equal to $\lambda/2$, not the full wavelength $\lambda$.

D.explanation: A node has zero displacement at all times, while a particle at an antinode oscillates with maximum amplitude.

hints: Focus on the words nodes and antinodes in the four statements - nodes stay at zero displacement while the loop between them moves as one shape.

Recall that at any instant the displacement envelope between two successive nodes is all on the same side of the equilibrium line, which tells you about phase, and that node to adjacent node is $\lambda/2$.
Compare each statement with those rules: check phase inside one loop, check antinode amplitude $2a$ against one-wave amplitude $a$, and check whether zero motion belongs to a node or an antinode.
walkthrough: Recall a stationary wave is formed by two progressive waves of same wavelength and amplitude travelling in opposite directions, giving fixed nodes of zero vibration and antinodes of maximum vibration.

Between two successive nodes there is one loop. At any time all displacements in that loop are in the same direction from equilibrium, reaching zero together and maxima together, so they oscillate in phase. Particles in the next loop move in the opposite direction, in antiphase.
Check amplitude: where the two waves of amplitude $a$ arrive in phase, at an antinode, the resultant amplitude is $a + a = 2a$, not $a$.
Check wavelength: one full wavelength $\lambda$ contains two loops, so the distance from one node to the next adjacent node is $\lambda/2$.
Check motion at special points: a node has zero displacement at all times, whereas a particle at an antinode oscillates with the largest displacement.
Therefore only the statement about all particles between two successive nodes oscillating in phase follows. This is option A.
